concepts.name: Electric charge and conservation
concepts.summary: Recall that charge comes in positive and negative kinds, is quantized in units of e, and is conserved in every process.

concepts.name: Conductors versus insulators
concepts.summary: Explain how charges move freely in conductors but not insulators and how objects become charged by friction, contact and induction.

concepts.name: Coulomb's law for point charges
concepts.summary: State and interpret the force between two point charges as proportional to the charges and inversely proportional to distance squared, attractive or repulsive by sign.

concepts.name: Electric field as force per charge
concepts.summary: Understand the electric field as the force per unit test charge and its direction as that of the force on a positive charge.

concepts.name: Electric field lines
concepts.summary: Read field line pictures to infer direction and relative strength of the field near charges and dipoles.

concepts.name: Magnets and magnetic poles
concepts.summary: Recall that magnets have two poles that attract or repel, that poles cannot be isolated, and that field lines run from north to south outside the magnet.

concepts.name: Currents create magnetic fields
concepts.summary: Explain that moving charges produce magnetic fields and describe the circular field around a straight wire using the right-hand rule.

misconceptions.text: Charge is created or destroyed when objects are rubbed together.
Electric field lines are the actual paths that charges follow.
Cutting a magnet in half yields separate north and south poles.

concepts.name: Superposition of electric forces
concepts.summary: Compute the net force or field from several point charges by adding vector components.

concepts.name: Electric potential energy and potential
concepts.summary: Calculate potential energy of charge pairs and potential of point charges as scalar quantities, and relate potential difference to work per charge.

concepts.name: Equipotentials and field relationship
concepts.summary: Sketch equipotentials and use the fact that the field points toward decreasing potential with magnitude equal to the potential gradient.

concepts.name: Capacitor and capacitance
concepts.summary: Calculate capacitance, charge, voltage and stored energy for a parallel-plate capacitor and for simple series and parallel combinations.

concepts.name: Magnetic force on moving charges
concepts.summary: Find the magnitude and direction of the force on a charge moving in a uniform magnetic field, including circular motion.

concepts.name: Magnetic force on current-carrying wires
concepts.summary: Compute the force on a straight wire in a uniform field and between two parallel currents.

concepts.name: Field of simple current geometries
concepts.summary: Use standard results for the field of a long straight wire, loop centre and ideal solenoid.

misconceptions.text: A point where the electric field is zero must also have zero potential.
A magnetic field does work on a moving charge and speeds it up.
A capacitor stores net charge, so total charge on it is Q.

concepts.name: Gauss's law applications
concepts.summary: Choose Gaussian surfaces to derive fields of spherical, cylindrical and planar charge distributions.

concepts.name: Fields from continuous distributions
concepts.summary: Integrate Coulomb's law over lines, rings and disks to obtain fields and potentials.

concepts.name: Conductors in electrostatic equilibrium
concepts.summary: Analyse why the field inside a conductor is zero, charge resides on the surface, and cavities are shielded.

concepts.name: Dielectrics in capacitors
concepts.summary: Analyse how a dielectric reduces the field, raises capacitance by factor κ, and changes energy under fixed charge or fixed voltage.

concepts.name: Biot-Savart law
concepts.summary: Integrate current elements to find magnetic fields of wire segments and loops.

concepts.name: Ampère's law applications
concepts.summary: Use symmetric Amperian loops to find fields of wires, solenoids and toroids.

concepts.name: Faraday's and Lenz's laws
concepts.summary: Calculate EMF from changing flux and determine induced current direction by opposing the change.

concepts.name: Motional EMF
concepts.summary: Analyse EMF in conductors moving through fields and relate it to flux change and magnetic force on charges.

misconceptions.text: Gauss's law only holds for symmetric charge distributions.
Induced EMF depends on the magnitude of the magnetic flux rather than its rate of change.
Ampère's law gives the field at the loop from only the current enclosed, ignoring other currents.

concepts.name: Differential forms of field laws
concepts.summary: Translate Gauss's, Faraday's and Ampère's laws between integral and differential form using divergence and curl.

concepts.name: Laplace and Poisson equations
concepts.summary: Set up electrostatic problems as potential equations with boundary conditions and appeal to uniqueness.

concepts.name: Method of images
concepts.summary: Evaluate when image charges replace induced surface charge and use them to solve conductor problems.

concepts.name: Displacement current
concepts.summary: Analyse why Ampère's law fails for a charging capacitor and how the changing electric flux term restores consistency.

concepts.name: Maxwell's equations as a system
concepts.summary: Interpret the four equations together, show they imply charge conservation, and identify the sources of each field.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic wave solutions
concepts.summary: Derive the vacuum wave equation and judge the transverse, speed-of-light plane-wave solutions it permits.

concepts.name: Inductance and magnetic energy
concepts.summary: Analyse self and mutual inductance and the energy stored in a magnetic field.

concepts.name: Fields in matter
concepts.summary: Distinguish free from bound charge and current, and use D and H with polarization and magnetization.

misconceptions.text: Displacement current is a flow of real charge across the capacitor gap.
The image charge physically exists behind the conducting plane and the field there is also given by the image solution.
Faraday's law only applies to loops of wire, not to empty space.

concepts.name: Potentials and gauge freedom
concepts.summary: Evaluate gauge choices for the scalar and vector potentials and show that physical fields are gauge invariant.

concepts.name: Poynting theorem and energy flow
concepts.summary: Use energy and momentum conservation in fields to assess power transport in circuits, waves and radiation pressure.

concepts.name: Radiation from accelerating charges
concepts.summary: Judge how retarded potentials lead to radiation fields and dipole radiation from accelerated charges.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic boundary conditions
concepts.summary: Apply interface conditions on E, D, B and H to derive reflection and transmission at material boundaries.

concepts.name: Relativistic unification of fields
concepts.summary: Construct the transformation of E and B between frames and the field tensor formulation showing magnetism as a relativistic effect.

concepts.name: Multipole expansion
concepts.summary: Construct multipole expansions of potentials to model localized sources and assess the dominant far-field term.

concepts.name: Modelling waves in media
concepts.summary: Design models of wave propagation in dispersive media, conductors and waveguides from Maxwell's equations with material response.

misconceptions.text: Potentials are only mathematical tools with no physical significance, since only fields matter.
Magnetic force is a separate fundamental interaction unrelated to relativity and electric force.
A charge moving at constant velocity radiates electromagnetic waves.
